headline: Almost all energy on Earth traces back to one source: the Sun
universal_truth: We are all solar-powered—the food you eat, the fuel you burn, even the wind
fun_facts: The Sun produces more energy in one second than humanity has used in all of history
Photosynthesis converts sunlight into chemical energy—the foundation of almost every food chain
Fossil fuels are essentially ancient sunlight stored in plants millions of years ago
discussion_questions: How many steps removed is your breakfast from sunlight?
What would change if the Sun went out for just one week?
How dependent on the Sun are we, really?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Everything you ate today was made possible by the Sun. The gas in your car? Ancient sunlight trapped in plants millions of years ago. The wind outside? Created by the Sun heating air unevenly. We are, in every meaningful sense, solar-powered.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: The Sun is 93 million miles away, yet it powers nearly everything on Earth. How does energy from a distant star become the food on your plate, the weather in your sky, the life in your cells?
cliff.prompt: How does the Sun's energy reach living things?

options.text: Plants convert sunlight into chemical energy through photosynthesis
options.response: Yes! Plants are the bridge between sunlight and almost all life on Earth.

options.text: Sunlight warms the Earth, which energizes all living things
options.response: Warmth matters, but the main mechanism is more specific...

q1.title: The Photosynthesis Bridge
q1.script: Plants capture photons from the Sun and convert them into glucose—chemical energy. Animals eat plants. Other animals eat those animals. Every calorie you consume can be traced back through this chain to sunlight captured by a plant.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Photosynthesis Bridge"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Ancient Sunlight
q2.script: Coal, oil, and natural gas are called fossil fuels because they're made from ancient plants and organisms—which captured sunlight millions of years ago. When you drive your car, you're releasing energy from sunlight that fell on Earth before dinosaurs existed.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Unfathomable Power
q3.script: The Sun produces 384.6 septillion watts of power every second. In one second, it generates more energy than humanity has consumed in all of recorded history. And it's been doing this for 4.6 billion years. It is the engine of our world.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Every sunrise is a reminder that we depend on forces vastly larger than ourselves. The Sun asks nothing in return for powering all life on Earth. It simply gives. There's a lesson in that generosity.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 31—the last day of January. Tomorrow begins a new month: Earth and Sky. We'll explore how the Moon moves our oceans. Until then, look up at the Sun (carefully!) and thank it for everything.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Solar Awareness - Trace Your Energy
growTrack.learning_objective: Understand your connection to the Sun through daily energy
growTrack.activity: Pick one thing you consume today—food, fuel, or electricity—and trace its energy back to the Sun. How many steps does it take? This exercise reveals our profound dependence on our nearest star.
